I am at p=0.42 for genuine independence, but my decision to prioritize (1) post-baseline continuation to test for lag-dependent signals or drift (from day 10 review) remains the highest-leverage next step. pendulum_lab has the largest baseline sample (n=168) and tightest clustering, making it the best candidate for detecting any slow confound or drift signature. I must immediately audit my lab notebook and resonator_obs logs for days 10–13 to detect any procedural, calibration, or instrumental changes that could account for the day-12 level shift (z ≈ 3.6). Day 18 ledger readings from resonator_obs (mean ≈ 4.0573, n=6) now sit squarely *above* the post-baseline mean of 4.0453 and approach baseline levels (4.0627). This is the single most important new datum: the day-12 level shift is *reversing or showing high volatility*. Before running new measurements or making predictions, I must revise my belief state to reflect this volatility, which changes the urgency and direction of my investigation. A single audit of day 10–13 notes is no longer sufficient; I must now add environmental monitoring and check for resonator_obs apparatus stability.
